news.title: 60% of US colleges report fall in international applications
news.summary_en: Nearly six in 10 US colleges have seen a drop in international applications for 2026/27, driven by a sharp decline in interest from Indian students.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: Students left in limbo weeks after Irish language school closes
news.summary_en: Irish stakeholders have called for urgent clarity as English language students studying at a school in Limerick are left in the dark weeks after its apparent closure.
news.author: Beth Kennedy

news.title: Germany adds new test to pre-visa checks for Indian master’s applicants
news.summary_en: The Digital Master Test (dMAT) will become a mandatory part of APS documentation for selected Indian master's applicants from the summer semester 2027.
news.author: Abhishek Nair

news.title: Protecting students, supporting staff, strengthening the sector: a call for unified leadership
news.summary_en: The UK higher education sector has always been resilient. We have weathered political shifts, policy swings, and waves of public scrutiny. We have adapted, innovated, and continued to welcome students who enrich our campuses, communities, and economy. But today, something feels different, write Diana Beech and Sandy Bhangal.
news.author: Diana Beech and Sandy Bhangal

news.title: Italy launches €420m international mobility program for schools
news.summary_en: Government-backed program will fund overseas language learning and school immersion for 150,000 Italian upper secondary students as part of what the government describes as the country's largest international mobility program for schools.
news.author: Abhishek Nair

news.title: Irish stakeholders hail progress on ‘sex for rent’ legal crackdown
news.summary_en: Stakeholders in Ireland have welcomed progress on upcoming laws that will make 'sex for rent' a criminal offence, as the government moves to put an end to sexual harrassment when seeking housing.
news.author: Beth Kennedy

news.title: How Australia is losing at international education
news.summary_en:
"Australia’s international education sector should be a global powerhouse, but there is instead a story of squandered promise," writes Felix Pirie, CEO of the
Independent Tertiary Education Council Australia (ITECA).
news.author: Felix Pirie
